01Rationale

Why this level matters

The last step is less about diagrams than about influence: making a case a board can fund, choosing what to build, buy or partner on, and growing a team of engineers and agents. This level is practice, built around one strategy you write and defend.

02Target competencies

Intended learning outcomes

Make the case

Write a business case and roadmap that a board can read in ten minutes.

Map the organisation

Build a capability map and decide what to build, buy or partner on.

Lead people and agents

Set up reviews, mentoring and working agreements for teams that include AI agents.

Defend your strategy

Present and answer hard questions about your own architecture strategy.

04Planned practical work

Your architecture strategy

Proposed project: Write an architecture strategy for a real or realistic organisation, then present it. This practical component will be developed and validated before the level opens.

The steps

  1. Describe the organisation and what it needs
  2. Draw the capability map
  3. Decide build, buy or partner for each gap
  4. Write the roadmap in three horizons
  5. Write the business case
  6. Write the board paper and prepare for questions

Intended validation criteria

  • Every roadmap item ties to a business need
  • Every build-or-buy choice states its cost and exit
  • The board paper fits on two pages

05How you learn

Proposed learning design

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The proposed learning design draws on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review; detailed learner materials will be published before release. Read the evidence and sources.

06Intended audience

What it builds on

Level 5, Architecture Governance and Evolution, or equivalent experience leading architecture work.
